title: IPsec: transport and tunnel modes, IKE and security associations

videos.script: Lesson 1 ended with a tunnel that anybody on the path could read. The ISP printed the request and the page that came back. {{plain}} IPsec fixes that without changing the idea. The packet still travels inside another packet. {{wrap}} What changes is the inside. It is encrypted, and every packet carries a check that only the other office could have made. {{esp}} Before one packet is protected, the two routers have to agree. Which algorithms, which keys, which networks. That conversation is called IKE, and it takes four messages. {{ike}} You will watch those four messages from the ISP's router. Then you will read the same exchange in the router's own log. {{log}} After that, you will look at what the agreement produced. Two security associations, one for each direction, each with its own number on the wire. {{sas}} Then you will break it on purpose. First with a wrong key, then with two offices that disagree about their networks. Each failure has its own message, and you will learn to tell them apart. {{fail}} Last comes a laptop at home, behind a router doing NAT. ESP cannot cross that router as it is, so it travels inside UDP. {{nat}}
